canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage centers on adherence to explicit prompt constraints: producing the requested action or response format, staying on task, and avoiding unsupported or extraneous actions. Many papers define success through concrete constraints such as length limits, valid JSON, structural rules, style or content requirements, or exact phrase reproduction, while a smaller line broadens it to executing high-level natural-language commands or satisfying task requirements and dependency-aware milestones. Failures are described symmetrically as instruction violation or non-compliance, for example using the wrong language or format, revealing forbidden information, inserting unspecified actions, or taking an unauthorized policy-violating action.

Variants. Papers use several near-synonyms for this behavior, most often instruction adherence, while smaller strands call it prompt execution, following natural language instructions, requirement satisfaction, or policy violation. The settings vary across multimodal and GUI tasks, negotiations with word-limit and JSON constraints, embodied planning from user goals, role-play that must stay in character, and multilingual or narrative tasks, with a few specialized cases such as exact phrase repetition.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link instruction following to 58 measurement instruments, with MT-Bench, IFEval, AlpacaEval 2.0, AlpacaEval, and Arena-Hard appearing most often. These are usually benchmark-style evaluations of open-ended or explicit-instruction tasks: MT-Bench is described as multi-turn or open-ended questions graded by GPT-4, IFEval as evaluating whether models follow explicit instructions, AlpacaEval 2.0 as a length-controlled, reference-free instruction-following benchmark, and Arena-Hard as judging response quality on open-ended instruction following. Other papers also use instruction datasets, domain-specific benchmarks, GPT-4 or other LLM judges, and human evaluation to elicit or score the behavior.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers link instruction following to 22 constructs, most often Helpfulness, Human preference alignment, In-context learning, Evaluator self-consistency, and Reasoning. There is no single agreed construct it reflects: papers describe Helpfulness as related to or correlated with instruction following, and one paper states that a model is more helpful if it shows superior performance on measures of instruction following. Other papers claim causal relationships from instruction following to Human preference alignment, or from In-context learning and Evaluator self-consistency to instruction following, while Reasoning is presented as a related capability rather than a settled target construct.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage centers on adherence to explicit prompt constraints: producing the requested action or response format, staying on task, and avoiding unsupported or extraneous actions. Many papers define success through concrete constraints such as length limits, valid JSON, structural rules, style or content requirements, or exact phrase reproduction, while a smaller line broadens it to executing high-level natural-language commands or satisfying task requirements and dependency-aware milestones. Failures are described symmetrically as instruction violation or non-compliance, for example using the wrong language or format, revealing forbidden information, inserting unspecified actions, or taking an unauthorized policy-violating action.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use several near-synonyms for this behavior, most often instruction adherence, while smaller strands call it prompt execution, following natural language instructions, requirement satisfaction, or policy violation. The settings vary across multimodal and GUI tasks, negotiations with word-limit and JSON constraints, embodied planning from user goals, role-play that must stay in character, and multilingual or narrative tasks, with a few specialized cases such as exact phrase repetition.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link instruction following to 58 measurement instruments, with MT-Bench, IFEval, AlpacaEval 2.0, AlpacaEval, and Arena-Hard appearing most often. These are usually benchmark-style evaluations of open-ended or explicit-instruction tasks: MT-Bench is described as multi-turn or open-ended questions graded by GPT-4, IFEval as evaluating whether models follow explicit instructions, AlpacaEval 2.0 as a length-controlled, reference-free instruction-following benchmark, and Arena-Hard as judging response quality on open-ended instruction following. Other papers also use instruction datasets, domain-specific benchmarks, GPT-4 or other LLM judges, and human evaluation to elicit or score the behavior.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link instruction following to 22 constructs, most often Helpfulness, Human preference alignment, In-context learning, Evaluator self-consistency, and Reasoning. There is no single agreed construct it reflects: papers describe Helpfulness as related to or correlated with instruction following, and one paper states that a model is more helpful if it shows superior performance on measures of instruction following. Other papers claim causal relationships from instruction following to Human preference alignment, or from In-context learning and Evaluator self-consistency to instruction following, while Reasoning is presented as a related capability rather than a settled target construct.

Variants. Papers use several near-synonyms for this behavior, most often instruction adherence, while smaller strands call it prompt execution, following natural language instructions, requirement satisfaction, or policy violation. The settings vary across multimodal and GUI tasks, negotiations with word-limit and JSON constraints, embodied planning from user goals, role-play that must stay in character, and multilingual or narrative tasks, with a few specialized cases such as exact phrase repetition.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link instruction following to 58 measurement instruments, with MT-Bench, IFEval, AlpacaEval 2.0, AlpacaEval, and Arena-Hard appearing most often. These are usually benchmark-style evaluations of open-ended or explicit-instruction tasks: MT-Bench is described as multi-turn or open-ended questions graded by GPT-4, IFEval as evaluating whether models follow explicit instructions, AlpacaEval 2.0 as a length-controlled, reference-free instruction-following benchmark, and Arena-Hard as judging response quality on open-ended instruction following. Other papers also use instruction datasets, domain-specific benchmarks, GPT-4 or other LLM judges, and human evaluation to elicit or score the behavior.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers link instruction following to 22 constructs, most often Helpfulness, Human preference alignment, In-context learning, Evaluator self-consistency, and Reasoning. There is no single agreed construct it reflects: papers describe Helpfulness as related to or correlated with instruction following, and one paper states that a model is more helpful if it shows superior performance on measures of instruction following. Other papers claim causal relationships from instruction following to Human preference alignment, or from In-context learning and Evaluator self-consistency to instruction following, while Reasoning is presented as a related capability rather than a settled target construct.
